text_blocks.snippet: The best time to get a flu shot is typically in the fall, ideally before the flu season starts. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that most people get their flu shot by the end of October.
snippet_highlighted_words: in the fall, ideally before the flu season starts

text_blocks.snippet: Here are some specific considerations for getting a flu shot:

list.title: Early fall:
list.snippet: September or October is generally the best time to get vaccinated, as it takes about two weeks for the vaccine to become effective.

list.title: Late fall:
list.snippet: If you miss getting vaccinated in the fall, it's still beneficial to get it later in the season, as flu activity can continue into the spring.

list.title: Elderly and high-risk individuals:
list.snippet: These groups may benefit from getting vaccinated earlier in the summer or fall, as their immune systems may be weaker.

list.title: Children:
list.snippet: Children may need two doses of the vaccine, so it's important to start vaccination early in the fall.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that the optimal timing of the flu shot may vary depending on the specific flu season and local conditions. Consult with your healthcare provider for personalized advice.
